pl590014.description: An ancient settlement on the island of Siphnos. The current church sits on Byzantine foundations and is surrounded by remains of older fortifications and other structures.

pl809327743.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl251542598.description: The Monastery of Saint John the Theologian (also known as the Monastery of Saint John the Divine) is a Greek Orthodox monastery dating to AD 1088 on the island of Patmos.

pl548453076.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl548453076.description: Metéora comprises a complex of six Eastern Orthodox monasteries built on natural sandstone pillars of the Thessalian plain. The site was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1988.

pl514403427.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl514403427.description: An eleventh-century monastery on Chios built by Constantine IX Monomachos. The site was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1990.

pl410249370.description: A fortified town in Laconia, Peloponnese, Greece, Mystras was named as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1989.

pl638120044.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl638120044.description: A medieval tower built ca. 1250 by the Frankish lord Guy I de la Roche.

pl451513645.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl451513645.description: One of the two known Genovese fortresses on Andros.

pl204230210.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl204230210.description: An Ottoman bridge at Oinoanda on the Xanthos river. A Latin inscription found nearby suggests an earlier Roman bridge existed at the site.

q533514.dateNote: Born in 1395 or 1396; sources differ (Britannica gives 1396).

q1113602.dateNote: The Knights Hospitaller began the castle in 1402 (some sources say 1404). The Ottomans took it in 1522.

q138302.died: 31 January 1556, Trinity Lavra of St. Sergius

q3320354.dateNote: Built from 1541 by two monks, the brothers Nektarios and Theophanes Apsaras. The year 1600 only stood for the 16th century.

q165425.summary: On 7 October 1571 a Holy League fleet led by Spain and Venice heavily defeated the Ottoman fleet in the Gulf of Patras.

pl194496209.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl194496209.description: Anavyssos, Greece, is the findspot of the kouros of Kroisos, a fallen warrior. The kouros dates ca. 530–520 B.C. and is housed in the National Archaeological Museum of Athens (inv. no. 3851). The kouros was discovered in 1936.

pl589729.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl590060.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl540783.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl540783.description: The strait between Euboea and Boeotia, located where the modern Greek city of Chalkida now stands. A bridge connected the land masses in antiquity.

pl543789.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl543789.description: An ancient settlement of Thessaly whose precise location is not known. It was probably near modern Prodromos Karditsas in Greece.

pl234032029.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl234032029.description: The Oropos Amphiareion clepsydra is a hydraulic inflow clock serving the Sanctuary of Amphiaraus. Situated on the southeast bank of the sacred spring of Amphiaraus, this inflow hydraulic clock dates to the 4th century BCE.

pl631385926.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl631385926.description: Modern name for an otherwise unnamed ancient settlement. It may have been a possession of the Ptolemies, Rhodes, and the Attalid kingdom, and was at least peripherally involved with Rome's war against Aristonikos as a Roman ally.

pl213924739.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl213924739.description: Palaikastro, located in eastern Crete, was an important trading center in antiquity, from the Bronze Age going forward.

pl306176341.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl448145858.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl448145858.description: The Sanctuary of Apollo at Halieis is a temple complex dedicated primarily to Apollo, constructed outside of the city of Halieis and dating between the seventh and fourth centuries BCE.

pl312809379.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl312809379.description: Korakou is a hill located on the Corinthian Gulf near New Corinth. It rises to 35 m above sea level. Carl Blegen conducted excavations at the site in 1915 and 1916. Archaeological remains show continuous use from the Early Helladic (EH) to Late Helladic periods (LH). It is suggested that the site served as a Mycenaean emporion. By the Archaic period the abandoned site gives way to burials.

pl29727643.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl29727643.description: An ancient sanctuary to Despoina located at Lykosoura, Arcadia.

pl599909.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl599909.description: An ancient temple of Poseidon, known today as the "Tomb of Homer", located on a height at the northern end of the Aegean island of Ios. Some funerary epigraphy has also been noted at the site.

pl741537853.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl741537853.description: Archaic temple to Artemis at Aulis, Boeotia. In mythology, said to be the place of death of Iphigenia. Mentioned in Euripides' 'Iphigenia at Aulis.'

q456079.placeNote: Where he was born is not recorded beyond the Mani; the pin is just the middle of Laconia.

pl194611949.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl194611949.description: The Tavşan Tepe Tümülüsü is a tumulus at Pergamon included in the UNESCO World Heritage site "Pergamon and its Multi-Layered Cultural Landscape".

pl921892403.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl921892403.description: Abundant archaeological evidence at modern Panagitsa in the modern Greek municipal unit of Elatia attests to an ancient settlement and associated cemetery in use from the Geometric period through at least Hellenistic times. Its ancient name is uncertain; various suggestions have been made in the literature.

pl841476129.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl841476129.description: The Square Peristyle is the modern name for a large square peristyle in the northeast corner of the Agora of Athens, begun around 300 BC, but never completed. It may have functioned as a lawcourt in the early Hellenistic period. It was demolished and used to build South Stoa II in the early 2nd century BC. The site was subsequently used for the Stoa of Attalos.

pl589666.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl599686.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0

pl235505945.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl235505945.description: The Kybele Sanctuary at Kapikaya is a rock-cut sanctuary sacred to Kybele, approximately 6 km from Pergamon, and is included in the UNESCO World Heritage site "Pergamon and its Multi-Layered Cultural Landscape".

pl643508013.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl643508013.description: The archaeological site of Tsoungiza shows evidence of human activity since the Early Neolithic period. Modern excavations began under Carl Blegen in 1924.

pl726345182.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl726345182.description: A country house in Attica dating to the fourth century BCE located near the fort and wall at Dema.

q368596.dateNote: 26 February 1916 (Wikidata P585, recorded to the day).

q228611.died: 6 March 1994, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center

cur-fossil-haua-fteah.dateNote: From 1951 to 1955 Charles McBurney dug this huge cave in Cyrenaica, Libya, down through 14 metres of layers, and two human jawbones turned up. People used the cave for over 100,000 years (more than 0.1 million years).
cur-fossil-haua-fteah.summary: A huge Libyan cave whose layers hold over 100,000 years of human life.

cur-fossil-apidima.dateNote: In 1978 a University of Athens team led by Theodoros Pitsios found two skulls in a cave at Apidima, in the Mani peninsula of southern Greece. In 2019 Katerina Harvati's team said one, Apidima 1, is a modern human about 0.21 million years old; the other looks Neanderthal, about 0.17 million years. The first date is still argued over.
cur-fossil-apidima.summary: A Greek cave with a skull that may be the oldest modern human found outside Africa.

pl792912222.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl792912222.description: Apidima Cave is located on the western shore of the Mani Peninsula in southern Greece. Archaeological excavation in the cave system has produced remains of both Neandertals and Homo sapiens dating to the Paleolithic. Cranial evidence from the cave suggests the presence of the earliest Homo sapiens known outside of Africa.

pl113317585.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl113317585.description: Chani Kokkonas is an archaeological site in Tempe valley, Thessaly, Greece. The excavations revealed remains of a Hellenistic complex with both ritual and workshop areas, as well as a Byzantine church and guesthouse (khan).

pl705163201.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl705163201.description: A sanctuary sacred to Poseidon on the island of Poros.

pl814953386.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl814953386.description: İkiz Tepe Tümülüsü (also Ikili Tumuli) is a tumulus near Pergamon that is included in the UNESCO World Heritage site "Pergamon and its Multi-Layered Cultural Landscape".

pl599856.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl599856.description: The largest bay of the island of Mykonos, opening to the north.

pl538278634.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl538278634.description: Through a series of survey and rescue excavations, the modern lignite mines just west of modern Megalopolis (and southwest of the ancient site of Megalopolis) in the Peloponnese have produced important evidence for ice age activity, especially at (but not limited to) a Lower Paeleolithic site known as Marathoussa 1.

pl482621854.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl482621854.description: The archaeological remains of a small Minoan settlement of approximately 12-20 houses on the island of Chryssi. Evidence for murex processing was discovered during excavations conducted in 2008.

pl463282370.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl463282370.description: Healing spring described by Pausanias on the Kytherios River, in Salmone, Elis.

pl570562.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl570562.description: An ancient settlement of Arcadia, possibly to be identified with modern Palaiomoiri.

pl573567.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl573567.description: From Hesiod onward, Greek writers locate the Nemean lion in a cave or ravine in this mountain and explain the mountain's name ("perforated") from being split by the ravine. Wiseman (in PECS, whence ToposText) identifies the Tretos as "the mountain on the W side of the main road between Kleonaia-Corinthia and Argolis" and the ravine as the modern Dervenakia pass. Camp in BAtlas silently suppresses this view, and mentioning "Tretos" only in a list of "unlocated" features in the map-by-map directory where he cites only Pausanias and glosses: "Corinthia-Argolis: pass, road".

pl252533527.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl252533527.description: A cave sanctuary, dedicated to Pan and the Nymphs, located near modern Ag. Marina in Phocis and therefore also near the site of Psilo Kastro (possibly ancient Patronis).

pl955675680.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl955675680.description: An ancient sanctuary of Artemis and Apollo associated with the ancient settlement of Abai and located near the modern Greek town of Kallipodi.

pl219059935.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl219059935.description: Tomb of Orestes described by Pausanias in the Agora of Sparta, near a Sanctuary of the Moirai. Supposedly housed the bones of Orestes.

pl308594948.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl308594948.description: A site on Ithaca that local tradition links to both Homer and Odysseus. Excavations in 1998 near the Church of St. Athanasius documented a series of walls including both Bronze Age and Iron Age phases, as well as a Hellenistic building constructed using orthostates, and a circular structure with a diameter of more than 7 meters.

pl306258361.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl306258361.description: Described by Pausanias as being on the road from Sparta to Arcadia.

cur-fossil-kocabas.dateNote: In 2002 workers at a travertine quarry at Kocabaş, near Denizli, Turkey, found pieces of a skull. John Kappelman's team showed it was Homo erectus. Later dating puts it at about 1.1–1.3 million years old.
cur-fossil-kocabas.summary: A Homo erectus skull from a quarry in Turkey, the oldest human fossil there.
